title: Opening and talk of Waffle Man's Call and Skaggs Leone
summary: Allen announces the recording at Tulane's Howard Tilton Library, gets Bourgeois's name (Wilfred, called Bill), then they discuss a 1924 record and Leone as an idol of Fazola.

story.theme_name: Starting the tape: names, dates and places
story.community_name: Interview openings: names, dates and tape setup

blocks.x: Okay, we'll do a little talking now. Let me see, I better put the place where we're recording. This is recorded at the Howard Tilton Library, Tulane University, and it's an interview with Bill Bourgeois, and today is December the 10th of 19... Okay, 1959. So we're gonna get your name on here first. All right. What is it? You mean my correct name? Well, you can give it if you want to.
It doesn't matter. Wilfred. Wilfred is your correct name. I've been called Bill ever since I was born, I guess.

Bill Bourgeois. And Florence, what's your name? You're taking pictures here. Florence, Florence. And I'm Dick Allen. Okay, let's see. We were just playing that Bosdell for a record of... Let's see, what was that? Waffle Man's Call? Waffle Man's Call. That's pretty old, isn't it? Yeah, 24, I think. And you said... That's about the year I started playing. Yeah, is that right? And you were saying he was good with the plunging music, huh?
Very, very good. He was excellent. And Skaggs, you say?
Skagg Leone, yeah. And what about him? We were talking about him and Fass, huh?
He was a very, very fine musician. And I think Fazzola was one of his... He was Fazzola's idol.
Yeah, I see. Sort of took after him. Yeah. And while we were talking, you mentioned Hank Kamen, one of the teachers here. You used to know him.
